state.misconception_label: Assumes that an arrow on a number line starts at zero

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: ![Number line with -12 and -7 marked. Starting at -12, follow an arrow pointing to the right labelled +10. Then there is an arrow labelled b pointing to the left, which ends at -7 on the number line.]() What is the value of \( b \) ? I got \( -7 \) because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: What would happen if you considered starting the arrow at -12 instead of zero in this problem?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I guess if I start at -12, then the +10 would take me to -2, right? But then I’m not sure how to figure out what \( b \) would be after that. Do I just go back from -2 to -7, or is there something else I should do?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let me ask you this: what would happen if you tried your method on a simpler version of the problem?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher effectively addresses the specific misconception about arrows starting at zero and maintains high cognitive demand, but Turn 3's suggestion to try a simpler problem feels like a step backward when the student had already made significant progress in Turn 2 toward understanding the correct approach.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently uses probing questions to guide the student's thinking without giving direct answers, which is a textbook example of the Socratic method.
